sections.h2: Where to record a deed in Ottawa County
sections.html:
Ottawa County runs its recording desk from West Olive, at 12220 Fillmore Street, West Olive, MI 49460. The building has a recording office in Room 146 and a combined vital records and deeds counter in Room 130, so phone ahead at (616) 994-4510 to learn which window takes your deed. The email is register@miottawa.org and the fax is (616) 994-4521.

A second site, the Research Library, is at 414 Washington Avenue, Room 115, in Grand Haven, the county seat. Its direct line is (616) 846-8109. Weekday service at both sites starts at 8 am and ends at 5 pm, though Grand Haven shuts for an hour after noon. On the third Monday of each month the vital records and deeds offices close from 8:00 to 9:30 am.

The Clerk and Register of Deeds operates five locations. Only West Olive and Grand Haven handle deeds, while Holland and Hudsonville are vital records sites.

Ottawa County records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt, as long as it meets the recording requirements. A fax or photocopy of a deed is turned away, because only originals with live signatures are accepted. Court papers must be certified by the court, and a death certificate must be certified by the Clerk's office before it can be recorded.

Professional filers use electronic recording. The county's software lets it record warranty deeds and other documents that need a tax stamp, and it accepts submissions from four approved companies, including Indecomm, Corporation Service Company and Simplifile. Contact each firm about eligibility and pricing. The county collects only the fees set by state and local law, and vendors may add processing charges.

A one-time filer can use the Consumer E-Recording portal for affidavits, liens, certificates of trust, mortgages, discharges, lis pendens, notices of commencement and releases. Deeds and other ownership transfers, UCC documents and foreclosure papers are barred from the consumer portal, so a seller has to deliver the deed in paper or through a title company.

At the counter you can pay in cash, by check or by card. Recording by card adds a 3% convenience fee, and copy orders can also draw on an escrow account.

Michigan sets the base amounts in MCL 600.2567, and Ottawa County adds its own online and card terms. Searching the index is free, and the county asks $1 per page, plus a convenience fee, to view, print or save an image.

Ottawa County recording and copy fees
ServiceAmount
Recording one document, any length$30
Extra instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3 each
Searching the online indexNo charge
Viewing, printing or saving an image online$1 per page plus a convenience fee
Certified copy$5 under the state schedule
Card payment when recording3% added

Copies are not obtained through Freedom of Information requests, since every record in the office is public or covered by statute and copy fees are fixed by state law. Anyone can get a copy of your deed once it is recorded.

Two statutes stack here: MCL 207.525 levies $3.75 per $500 for the state, and MCL 207.504 levies 55 cents per $500 for the county, the rate for any county under 2,000,000 people. Any remainder under $500 is treated as a full block. The deed needs to show the value or carry an affidavit, and the seller is the party who owes the tax.

The median owner-occupied home in Ottawa County is valued at $323,400, so for a typical sale the tax is a real line item on the settlement statement. Ask your title company for the figure before you set a net-proceeds target.

You can often avoid the tax with an exemption written on the deed. The common ones for homeowners are:

  • Consideration under $100.
  • Mortgage foreclosure deeds, including deeds in lieu, under the state act.
  • Gifts down the family line, parent to child or grandparent to grandchild, which the state act alone excuses.
  • A spouse's deed that makes or ends a tenancy by the entireties.
  • A deed whose only job is to cure a flaw in title the grantee already holds.

The Document Recording page on the county site links both a County Exemptions sheet and a State Exemptions sheet.

The office does not draft documents, supply forms or give legal advice, and it does not furnish abstracts of title. Use an attorney, title company or real estate agent for help. The office cannot say when a house was built or whether a survey exists either, since it only holds land records, and most property has never had a survey recorded.

A state law effective April 1, 1997 requires 2.5 inches at the top and half an inch on the other sides, to leave room for recording stamps. MCL 565.201 contains that rule. Witnesses are no longer required on documents, though most documents still need a notary.

Papers that need a tax certificate from the Treasurer's office:

  • Warranty deeds.
  • Land contracts and assignments of land contracts.
  • Master deeds and amendments to master deeds.

MCL 211.135 backs that requirement and excuses quitclaim deeds without covenants of warranty. If a house is in mortgage foreclosure, the Register of Deeds takes redemption payments, though you may redeem straight through the lender or its lawyer. After the redemption period runs out, only the lender can help.

The county also offers Property Fraud Alerts. Owners sign up to be told when a document is recorded that affects their property.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Ottawa County
sections.html:
Ottawa County is in West Michigan on 24 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. Holland is the largest city, and the others include Zeeland, Hudsonville, Coopersville and Ferrysburg. Grand Valley State University is in Allendale and Hope College is in Holland, which keeps demand for rentals and starter homes steady near both campuses.

Population is estimated at 308,459, up 4.1% from the 2020 count of 296,200. The median home value is $323,400, the owner-occupied rate is 79.3%, median gross rent is $1,211 and median household income is $90,502. Building permits numbered 1,411 in 2025, so new construction competes with resale listings.

Most sellers never visit the recording office, because the title company handles it. If you are closing without one, work through this order.

  1. Confirm the deed carries original signatures and a notary acknowledgment.
  2. Check the margins, the grantee address and the drafter's name.
  3. Ask the Treasurer's office for the tax certificate if the deed is a warranty deed or land contract.
  4. Write the value or an exemption on the deed.
  5. Bring the original to West Olive or Grand Haven, with the $30 fee and the transfer tax.

A cash sale uses the same steps. It skips the lender, so the recording timeline of one to two days often sets the closing date. Call (616) 994-4510 if you are unsure which window to use.

faqs.q: Where does a deed get recorded in Ottawa County?
faqs.a: Bring it to the recording office at 12220 Fillmore Street in West Olive, or let a title company e-record it. Phone (616) 994-4510 to confirm the room. The Washington Avenue site in Grand Haven is the research library.

faqs.q: Can I record a photocopy or fax of a deed in Ottawa County?
faqs.a: No. Staff record only papers bearing original signatures.

faqs.q: How quickly does Ottawa County record a deed?
faqs.a: The county records and returns a document within one to two days of receipt when it meets the recording requirements. A title company or lender decides when the original reaches you.

faqs.q: Can I use the Ottawa County consumer e-recording portal for my deed?
faqs.a: No. The portal excludes deeds and other documents that transfer ownership, as well as UCC documents and foreclosure papers. It handles items like mortgages, discharges and notices of commencement.

faqs.q: Who pays Ottawa County transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The state charges $3.75 and the county charges 55 cents for each $500 of value, unless an exemption written on the deed applies.
